messages:
Jordan (Acme): Hey folks — hitting a bunch of 413s when streaming large embedding batches to /v1/embeddings. Trying to upload ~50k texts by streaming chunked requests (python generator), chunks ~5k vectors each. Started seeing 413s after a few minutes. Any quick tips? :anguished:

Emma (Support): Sorry you're blocked — can you paste a minimal repro and the exact error response? Which model and embedding dim are you using? Also include the request_id from the response headers if present.

Jordan (Acme): Here's a trimmed curl we used for streaming (we do Transfer-Encoding: chunked):

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Transfer-Encoding: chunked" \
  --data-binary @chunks.ndjson
```

chunks.ndjson looks like:
```
{"input": "...text1..."}\n
{"input": "...text2..."}\n
... (newline-delimited vectors) ...
```

Response we get repeatedly: HTTP/1.1 413 Request Entity Too Large
{
  "error": "RequestEntityTooLarge",
  "message": "payload too large for this endpoint"
}
Request-ID: rwd_abcdef123456

Model: embed-large-v1 (dim=1024). We also sometimes see a short 400 with "dimension mismatch: expected 1024 got 768" but 413 is most common.

Devon (Eng-Oncall): 413 usually means a gateway/proxy or our front-end limit intercepts the request size. A few quick things to check: 1) Are you going through a customer proxy or CDN (CloudFront, Fastly)? They often have 4MB default body limits. 2) If you set Content-Length incorrectly with chunked, some proxies will choke — prefer omitting Content-Length when using Transfer-Encoding: chunked. 3) Lower chunk size: target <= 1MB per HTTP chunk (uncompressed) and aim for ~500-1000 vectors per chunk for 1024-dim vectors.

Maria (SRE): Also note our internal ingress has a default max body of 8MB per request unless the private deployment was configured differently. If your request arrives via a load balancer with a stricter limit, it will return 413 before it hits our app tier. Check any intermediate nginx/nginx.conf or API gateway settings. If you can share a tcpdump or the request headers we can confirm.

Emma (Support): For a reproducible workaround while we debug infra limits: 1) switch to smaller NDJSON chunks, e.g., 800 vectors per chunk for 1024-dim; 2) add a short sleep between chunks or limit concurrency; 3) include an idempotency_key per-chunk so retries are safe; 4) capture the full response headers (Request-ID, X-Proxy-Info) and paste them here. Example python generator we recommend:

```python
# yield chunks as newline-delimited JSON strings
BATCH = 800
for i in range(0, len(texts), BATCH):
    chunk = "\n".join(json.dumps({"input": t}) for t in texts[i:i+BATCH]) + "\n"
    yield chunk.encode('utf-8')
```

Devon (Eng-Oncall): Also watch for dimension mismatch. Some pipelines preprocess (e.g., older embed model with dim=768) and accidentally mix vectors. If the service sees mixed dims in a single bulk request we sometimes return a 400; but dimension errors are distinct from 413. If you saw both, double-check the producer that builds chunks — ensure model and vectorizer match.

Jordan (Acme): FYI we are behind our corporate proxy. I pushed a test that drops chunks to ~700 vectors and removed Content-Length. Immediately fewer 413s. I got one 413 with Request-ID rwd_ghijk7890 and one 400 dimension mismatch rwd_lmnop456 — attaching the response headers snippet.

DeployBot: Incident created: INC-2026-842 (auto): "Customer streaming embeddings 413s via corporate proxy" — severity P2. Assigned to infra-proxy-team.

Maria (SRE): Good find. If the proxy is the root cause, ask your infra team to raise body size or allow chunked streaming. If they can't change it, stick to smaller chunks and parallelize multiple connections (e.g., 8 concurrent uploads of 700-vector chunks) to recover throughput. For throughput tuning: 8 workers x 700 vectors x 1.5ms/vector ~ target throughput, adjust for network.

Emma (Support): For completeness, if you need a server-side workaround, we can accept multipart uploads to our object ingest (if available in your plan) and do server-side batching into embeddings. That avoids single big requests. I'll open a support ticket with options.

Jordan (Acme): Thanks — reducing to 700/ chunk + 6 concurrent uploads seems stable and avoids 413. Throughput is down ~20% but acceptable for now. I'll forward proxy contact details so infra-proxy-team can coordinate config changes. Appreciate the quick help! :thumbsup:
